projets.pitch: A real-time strategy game in the browser, on a world map with no edges, played solo against bots or online with friends.
projets.probleme: Delivering an online multiplayer service end to end: rules written from scratch, a deterministic game engine, a server that relays orders without computing the game, and production on my own server, isolated from the rest of the site. Version 1.0 ended the beta in November 2026; 1.1 adds a 3D globe that players can switch on.
projets.role: Author and maintainer: rules specification, architecture, development, testing and running the public server.
points_forts: Every player runs the same simulation: the server only numbers the orders, ten turns per second.
A read-only container with no privileges and no Internet access, deployed by a dedicated key that can run a single command.
Playing needs no account and no cookie; the server keeps only anonymous counters, and optional accounts are stored as hashes.
Tested in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit on every change, with at least 90% of lines covered, CodeQL, an image scan and OpenSSF Scorecard.
Rules written from scratch, under a clean-room policy enforced by continuous integration, with first outside contributions merged.

projets.titre: Zeus + Poseidon on Mac and Linux
projets.pitch: Running a 2000 Windows game on Macs and Linux, from its original code, with no Wine and no virtual machine.
projets.probleme: Zeus: Master of Olympus is a 32-bit Windows game that Apple Silicon Macs can no longer run. The usual answers are Wine or a virtual machine. This project runs the game's original code inside a small sandboxed x86 emulator and rewrites the Windows functions it needs as native code. It now runs on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, and on x86-64 and arm64 Linux.
projets.role: Author and maintainer: reverse engineering, architecture, development, testing, releases and community.
points_forts: The real game, not a remake: same simulation, same save files, from the first tutorial to the adventure editor.
Accuracy you can check: ten replayed scenarios compare every frame and the whole game state, tick by tick, with the original game.
The game's file formats documented, with reference readers in Python.
A public roadmap towards a fully native engine, one part at a time.
Ready-to-run apps for four platforms, with no game files in the repository.

projets.pitch: This website, run as a project in its own right: open source, self-hosted and secure by design.
projets.probleme: Showing how I run a project and handle security, rather than describing it. The code is public; only the private area's content stays on the server.
projets.role: Scoping, architecture, security, development and operations.
points_forts: A roadmap in milestones, each with a checkable exit criterion.
Strict nonce-based CSP, HSTS and DNSSEC: A+ on Mozilla Observatory and SSL Labs, checked by an automated audit.
CI with CodeQL, Dependabot and Docker image scanning.
Personal private links that expire and can be revoked, encrypted off-site backups.
projets.contribuer: Report a vulnerability privately as described in the security policy, or open an issue for a mistake on the site.

projets.pitch: Taking over a wealth management firm's website and automating its publishing.
projets.probleme: A 187-page static site with no templates, edited by hand and uploaded over FTP. Any change to the menu or contact details had to be repeated on every page.
projets.role: Webmaster: site audit, checking tools, automated publishing.
points_forts: Automatic publishing to the host on every approved change.
A checker for links, images, sitemap and search index.
A backup before every change, with a documented rollback.
